articles.title: Hokit vs. Jon Jones? I've Got My Answer
articles.description: Chael Sonnen answers fan questions on another edition of Ask Uncle Chael, including one of the biggest heavyweight debates: who would win between Josh Hokit and Jon Jones? Chael makes his pick—and reveals that Hokit and Jones have actually trained together. He explains what he knows about Jones' training camp, why those private rounds matter, and what both men may already know about a potential matchup. Plus, Chael discusses reality TV, who should play him in a movie, Matt Lindland, Anderson Silva's barbecue invitation, his loss to Anderson, and why conditioning matters more than almost anything else in fighting.

articles.title: Ciryl Gane's Wins Keep Adding to Jon Jones' Legacy #ufc
articles.description: Every time Ciryl Gane wins, it adds another chapter to the Jon Jones heavyweight legacy debate. Chael Sonnen points out that nobody can deny how dominant Jon Jones was during the opening four minutes of their fight. Whether you're a supporter or a critic of Jones, that performance remains part of the conversation whenever Gane competes. But Josh Hokit has his own legacy to build. If he captures the heavyweight championship, he wants to make sure there's no question about the legitimacy of his reign. The goal isn't just to win the belt—it's to become an undisputed champion and separate himself from the debate surrounding previous heavyweight titleholders. Chael examines the connection between Gane, Jones, and the next generation of heavyweight contenders. #JonJones #CirylGane #JoshHokit #UFC #Heavyweight #MMA #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Should the UFC Sign Usman Nurmagomedov?
articles.description: Should the UFC sign Usman Nurmagomedov after what happened with Merab Dvalishvili in Abu Dhabi? Chael Sonnen looks at whether Usman's involvement should affect his future with the UFC or another major promotion. Merab says he has forgiven him, Usman has already faced serious consequences, and the incident unexpectedly helped turn Saba into a name people now want to see compete. Chael argues that acknowledging Usman's actions were wrong doesn't necessarily mean a promotion needs to punish him again, and he explains why the right response to someone who's already been punished is sometimes to help him back up.

articles.title: Did Josh Hokit Get Punished for Being Tough? #ufc
articles.description: Did Josh Hokit get punished for being tough? Chael Sonnen questions why Josh wasn't given the same opportunity for recovery after an accidental eye poke that a fighter would receive following a low blow. He points to Joe Rogan's discussion of the incident and argues that the rules shouldn't depend on how much punishment a fighter is willing to endure. Chael also compares the situation to Tom Aspinall's fight with Ciryl Gane, where an eye poke prevented Aspinall from continuing and a rematch was subsequently discussed. If an accidental foul makes one fighter unable to continue, why should the outcome be different simply because another fighter fights through it? Chael explains why he believes Hokit has a legitimate argument for a rematch—and why toughness shouldn't end up working against a fighter. #UFC #JoshHokit #CirylGane #TomAspinall #MMA #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Jake Paul Has a Problem
articles.description: Jake Paul believes bringing Khabib Nurmagomedov back for one fight could help change the fight business. Chael Sonnen isn't convinced. After Jake asked Khabib what it would take to compete again—including floating a hypothetical $200 million figure—Chael explains why everyone trying to lure Khabib back has focused on the wrong thing. According to Chael, money wasn't the biggest issue behind Khabib walking away. But Chael's bigger problem is Jake's belief that signing one massive star, or simply treating fighters better, can fundamentally change the industry. From the IFL to PFL and MVP, Chael looks at why the "fighter-first" approach hasn't translated into audience demand and questions what Khabib could actually change.

articles.title: Josh Hokit Deserves More Respect #ufc
articles.description: Josh Hokit may have lost to Ciryl Gane, but Chael Sonnen believes there's a lot more to take away from that fight than the result. Hokit was the undersized heavyweight, facing the very size and strength advantage that many believed would make Gane such a difficult matchup. He took the shots, battled through the pressure, got lifted off the canvas, and still gave Gane a tremendous fight. Chael believes Josh deserves enormous credit for his competitive spirit and performance. But he also has a message for Hokit fans: supporting Josh doesn't mean tearing down Ciryl Gane. Gane won a hard-fought fight, and both men deserve recognition. Chael explains why there's plenty to celebrate on both sides and why an immediate rematch isn't necessarily the answer. #JoshHokit #CirylGane #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews

articles.title: Bruce Buffer is Wrong
articles.description: Chael Sonnen explains why the viral moment between Josh Hokit and Bruce Buffer wasn't nearly as serious as some are making it out to be. According to Chael, Buffer took a small shot at Hokit first. Hokit responded with a middle finger, an equal and opposite reaction known in the locker room as a "receipt." At that point, they were square. The problem, according to Chael, is what happened afterward. He explains the unwritten locker room code, why Hokit's response was appropriate, and why Buffer should have simply let the issue end there.

articles.title: Josh Hokit Is Doing EXACTLY What He Should With Jon Jones
articles.description: Chael Sonnen explains why Josh Hokit is doing exactly the right thing by going directly at Jon Jones. For years, the heavyweight division has lived under the shadow of the unanswered question about Jon Jones. Francis Ngannou never settled it. Tom Aspinall may always be asked what would have happened. Alex Pereira understood the problem and called Jones out directly. Now it's Josh Hokit's turn. Chael explains why Hokit calling out Jones isn't disrespect; it's actually a sign of respect, and why Hokit needs to make it clear that if Jones wants to test him, he's ready.

articles.title: The biggest part of Gane vs Hokit #ufc
articles.description: The fight was over, but one of the biggest moments of the night came after the final bell. Chael Sonnen reveals how badly he wanted to see Josh Hokit shake Ciryl Gane's hand after their fight. Josh stood up, accepted the handshake, and showed the kind of respect Chael believes should always be part of the sport. Win or lose, fighters compete, shake hands, walk away, and move on. That's how the game should be played. Chael was extremely proud of Hokit for that moment and makes it clear that praising Josh doesn't mean taking anything away from Ciryl Gane. He appreciated the entire event and believes the post-fight sportsmanship deserves just as much attention as what happened inside the Octagon. #JoshHokit #CirylGane #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #Sportsmanship

articles.title: Usman Nurmagomedov's Out of Jail (Chael Breaks Down the Brawl)
articles.description: Chael Sonnen takes a closer look at the wild Merab Dvalishvili-Usman Nurmagomedov incident in Abu Dhabi—and the unexpected star who emerged from it. Saba was virtually unknown before the altercation. A week later, his social following had exploded, and even Dana White was discussing him. Chael breaks down the footage, Usman's surprisingly impressive technique during the melee, and how the smallest guy involved suddenly became one of the biggest stories from the incident. There may have been no heroes that night. But if there was one, Chael knows who it was.

articles.title: Did the Judges Get the Josh Hokit Fight Wrong? #ufc
articles.description: Did the judges get the Josh Hokit fight wrong? Chael Sonnen isn't ready to call it a robbery, even though many people watching believed Hokit had done enough to win. Chael discusses the reaction to the scorecards, including the criticism directed at Daniel Cormier's interpretation of the fight. But the bigger conversation goes beyond one controversial decision. How should judges actually score an MMA fight? How much weight should be given to damage, aggression, and effective techniques? Chael has a clear opinion: it's time to simplify the UFC's scoring criteria. He believes damage and octagon control should be removed, leaving judges with just three words to guide their decisions: Effective combat techniques. It's a proposal that could change how fans, fighters, and judges look at every UFC fight. #UFC #JoshHokit #MMAScoring #UFCJudging #MMA #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Was Josh Hokit Robbed? #ufc
articles.description: Was Josh Hokit robbed? Chael Sonnen admits he initially had Josh winning four rounds to none heading into the fifth, but after having more time to reflect, he's not ready to call the result a robbery. Chael explains why he was so impressed with Hokit. Giving up 17 pounds, Josh walked his opponent down, smothered him, and showed qualities that deserve plenty of recognition regardless of the final result. But does the fight deserve an immediate rematch? Chael doesn't think so. Instead, he has a much bigger prediction for Josh Hokit: Alex Pereira could be next. And if that matchup gets announced, Chael believes fans are going to go crazy. #UFC #JoshHokit #AlexPereira #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews

articles.title: UFC 334 Scorecard Chaos: How Kevin Holland vs Uros Medic Became a Draw
articles.description: What really happened with the Kevin Holland vs Uros Medic scorecards at UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden. Bruce Buffer read the cards as 30-27, 29-28, 28-28 for a majority draw. The official scores were 28-28 (Michael Bell), 28-28 (Chris Lee) and 29-27 Medic (David Bruce). Medic lost a point in round two for low blows, and the deduction counted on all three cards. The difference was round one: Bell and Lee gave it to Holland, Bruce gave it to Medic despite Holland's knockdown. articles.title: ‘Shout Out Saba!’ Izzy & DJ React to Merab Getting Jumped
Gane vs Hokit: Robbery?  Fighters React to  the Eye Poke
articles.description: Gane vs Hokit: Robbery? Fighters React to the Eye Poke Ciryl Gane kept the UFC heavyweight title with a unanimous decision (48-47 x3) over Josh Hokit at UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden - and the fight world could not agree on what it just watched. An uncalled first-round eye poke, Hokit saying he "saw triple the whole fight," an "immediate rematch" request, Alex Pereira telling Hokit "for me, you won," Dana White's scorecard, and a weekend-long war of words between Josh Hokit and Jon Jones. Reactions from Dana White, Sean O'Malley, Demetrious Johnson, Alexander Volkanovski, Alex Pereira, Daniel Cormier, Michael Bisping, Henry Cejudo, Brendan Schaub, Ariel Helwani, Alexander Volkov, Israel Adesanya, Francis Ngannou and Jon Jones. Note: Hokit's complaints are his own claims; we found no post in which he called Gane a cheater, and no public response from Gane at time of publishing. articles.title: Jon Jones and Josh Hokit Go to War on Social Media After UFC 334
articles.description: Jon Jones and Josh Hokit went to war on social media hours after UFC 334. Ciryl Gane beat Hokit by unanimous decision, 48-47 on all three cards, in Hokit's fifth UFC fight. Jones, who had let Hokit train in his camp in Albuquerque, posted that almost every fighter who talks crap about him ends up losing the next fight. Hokit quoted that post and went off.
